assets.name: terrain
assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original production pixel art for Syntax Forest, the second region of Glitchlands, an educational top-down monster-catching debugging adventure. Retro 16-bit handheld RPG aesthetic, orthographic top-down with slight frontal faces, crisp square pixels and dark 1-pixel outlines, restrained palette of deep pine #173c32, moss #53754c, teal #4b8b81, plum #41364f, warm amber #e9ba69, cream #f2e5bd. Chunky readable silhouettes. Not any existing franchise or asset pack. No text, letters, labels, logos, numbers, watermarks, grid lines, perspective mockups, or decorative sheet borders. All cells exact and equally spaced, no sprite overlaps. Asset type: seamless terrain texture atlas. EXACT 1024x1024 square canvas, 8 columns x 8 rows of 128x128-pixel cells, no gutters. Each cell depicts one 16x16 logical pixel tile enlarged exactly 8x nearest-neighbor, so features are chunky 8px squares. Fill each cell completely. Rows 1-2: 16 subtle repeatable forest floor tiles: dark grass, moss, ferns, leaf litter, roots, earth, pale path soil, fungal soil. Rows 3-4: 16 dirt path tiles: center, straight horizontal, straight vertical, four corners, T junctions, cross, ends, stones, trail edge variations. Rows 5-6: 16 pond and stream tiles: teal still water, rippled water, bank edge north east south west, four corners, reeds and wet soil. Rows 7-8: 16 additional seamless tiles: dark canopy cover, stone paving, cliff faces and upper edges, wood bridge deck horizontal and vertical, plank floor, glitched moss as a subtle violet accent. Align boundaries for repeatable center textures. Functional texture atlas, not an illustrated map.
